title: The Contemporary session with Benny Carter, Shelly Manne and Andre Previn
summary: Dance recalls 'They Raided the Joint' and 'I Cried for You', then the Contemporary album Humes calls one of her best sessions, with Benny Carter finding the musicians. Previn later asked, through Koenig, to be on her next date.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: that was just a period there, in your career that, you know, it was a slower period in your career. I mean that's how people's careers go, up and down and around bout. So really, actually, well I'll tell you what Helen, you did make some good records, you know. In '52 you made that "They Raided The Joint" and that did well.

And "I Cried For You". There is one, and you tell me about this because I know this meant something to you, you made that album with Benny Carter, Shelly Manne, and Andre Previn, for Contemporary. And you enjoyed that, didn't you?
I certainly did. That was one of the best sessions I ever had.
Yeah. You know everybody was relaxed and you didn't have to worry about nothing.
I could sing the songs and I didn't have to worry about the musicians.
Yeah, that's right. Was it Benny
